hints.content:
###The strategy

We want to rewrite one of the exponential terms in the equation so that the bases of the two terms are the same.  Then, we will be able to equate the exponents and solve for $x$. [[☃ explanation 2]]

options.explanation: If $a^m=a^n$, then $m=n$. So equating the bases allows us to equate the exponents.

hints.content:
###Matching the bases

Let's rewrite $\left(\dfrac{1}{49}\right)\^{\Large 2x+9}$ so its base is $7$.

$\begin{align}\left(\dfrac{1}{49}\right)\^{\Large2x+9}&=  (7^{-2})\^{\Large 2x+9} &&&&\text{Rewrite }\dfrac{1}{49}\text{ as }7^{-2}\\\\
 &=7\^{\Large -2(2x+9)}&&&&\text{Since }(a^n)^m=a^{n\cdot m} \\\\
&=7\^{\Large -4x-18}\end{align}$

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Yes! We can choose any base we want. As long as the base is the same on both sides of the equality, we can equate the exponents and solve for the unknown.

For example, we can convert the left side of the original equation into base $\dfrac{1}{49}$ as follows:

$\begin{align}7\^{\Large 3-5x}&=\left(\left(\dfrac{1}{49}\right)\^{\Large -\frac12}\right)\^{\Large 3-5x}&\text{(since } 7 \text{ is the square root of } 49)\\\\
&=\left(\dfrac{1}{49}\right)\^{\Large -\frac{3-5x}{2}}\end{align}$

hints.content:
###Solving the linear equation

We obtained the following equation.

$7\^{\Large 3-5x}=7\^{\Large -4x-18}$

Now we can equate the exponents and solve for $x$.

$\begin{align}
3-5x&=-4x-18\\\\\\
x &=21\end{align}$

[[☃ explanation 2]]

###The answer###

The answer is $x=21$.

*You can check this answer by substituting $\it{x=21}$ in the original equation and evaluating both sides.*
